content: Furthermore, the convergence of physical security and information technology is particularly pronounced in the commercial domain. The IT security conference held at the Sandton Convention Centre in June 2026 served as a critical meeting point for South African security providers and client organizations across diverse sectors, underscoring the vital importance of cross-sector collaboration and networking in the country's IT security landscape [23] . The contemporary market is characterized by a definitive shift away from traditional, purely physical security measures toward modern, holistic systems that seamlessly blend human personnel with advanced technological capabilities [Sources 1,2]. Technologies such as artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, unmanned aerial vehicles or drones, and smart security devices are now at the forefront of industry standard practices, reshaping how security providers operate and deliver value to their clients [Sources 1,2]. It is important to recognize that while these figures represent a longer-term forecast, they underscore the persistent dynamism and lucrative nature of this market, even as continuous innovations reshape daily operational practices [Sources 1,2,4]. The private security sector represents a substantial component of this expanding market and has experienced notable growth fueled directly by technological integration [Source 2]. A primary catalyst for this market evolution has been the widespread adoption and integration of next-generation technologies, most notably artificial intelligence and cloud-based security services. A defining milestone in this context was the issuance of the executive order titled "Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security" by the White House on June 2, 2026 [51] . This pivotal directive underscores a definitive governmental commitment to harmonizing the rapid development of artificial intelligence with the implementation of robust security measures. Furthermore, high-level discourse at the CNAS 2026 National Security Conference highlighted that artificial intelligence, drone technology, and other cutting-edge innovations are fundamentally reshaping national security and broader economic strategies [54] . Innovations such as zero trust architectures and advanced Internet of Things security perimeter management continue to be of paramount significance in fortifying digital borders against unauthorized access and lateral movement within networks [55] .
